'''Ellen Kovner Silbergeld''' (born 1945)<ref>[http://nrs.harvard.edu/urn-3:RAD.SCHL:sch00906 Ellen K. Silbergeld Papers]</ref> is a leading American expert in the field of environmental health.

==Background==

Elizabeth Kovner was born in 1945. Her parents were [[Joseph Kovner]], a lawyer (then with the [[Congress of Industrial Organizations]]) and Mary Helen Gion. She has two siblings.<ref>
{{cite news
| title = Obituaries: Mary Helen Gion Kovner
| newspaper = Washington Post

| date = 5 September 1992
| accessdate = 23 September 2017}}</ref><ref>

| publisher = Infobase Publishing
| url = https://books.google.com/books?id=uPRB-OED1bcC
| pages = 667–668
| date = 2007
| isbn = 9781438118826
| accessdate = 23 September 2017}}</ref><ref>
{{cite web

| publisher = Schlesinger Library, Radcliffe Institute, Harvard University
| url = http://nrs.harvard.edu/urn-3:RAD.SCHL:sch00906
| date = 2007
| accessdate = 23 September 2017}}</ref>

After graduating from [[Vassar College]] [[summa cum laude]] in 1967,<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://scienceweb.vassar.edu/women/ |title=Women in Science - Hall of Fame |access-date=2010-04-16 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100308211644/http://scienceweb.vassar.edu/women/ |archive-date=2010-03-08 |url-status=dead }}</ref> she earned a [[Ph.D.]] in [[environmental engineering]] at [[Johns Hopkins University]] in 1972.<ref name=faculty>{{Cite web |url=http://faculty.jhsph.edu/default.cfm?F=Ellen&L=Silbergeld |title=Johns Hopkins Bloomberg School of Public Health Faculty - Ellen Silbergeld |access-date=2010-04-16 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100613213516/http://faculty.jhsph.edu/default.cfm?f=Ellen&l=Silbergeld |archive-date=2010-06-13 |url-status=dead }}</ref>

==Career==

She is a professor at the [[Bloomberg School of Public Health]] at [[Johns Hopkins University]] and used to be on the faculty at the [[University of Maryland, Baltimore]].<ref name=faculty/> Before that she worked as a scientist for [[Environmental Defense]].<ref name=faculty/> She was editor-in-chief of the journal ''[[Environmental Research]]''<ref>[http://www.elsevier.com/wps/find/journaleditorialboard.cws_home/622821/editorialboard#editorialboard ''Environmental Research'' - Editorial Board]</ref> she serves on many other editorial boards
She is an authority on the toxicological manifestations of [[lead poisoning|lead]] and [[mercury poisoning]], having done some of the first research on how lead affects the central nervous system. Silbergeld has also been involved in public policy and raised public awareness of the dangers of lead. Her current research focuses on the role is food animal production in the selection and dissemination of [[antimicrobial resistance]]. She has written a book on this topic, ''Chickenizing Farms and Food'' published by [[Johns Hopkins University Press]] in 2016.

In 1993, she received the prestigious [[MacArthur Fellows Program|MacArthur Fellowship]] ("genius award") from the [[MacArthur Foundation]].<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.macfound.org/site/c.lkLXJ8MQKrH/b.1142799/k.9651/Fellows_List__S.htm |title=MacArthur Foundation - Fellows List: S |access-date=2006-08-11 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20060928181050/http://www.macfound.org/site/c.lkLXJ8MQKrH/b.1142799/k.9651/Fellows_List__S.htm |archive-date=2006-09-28 |url-status=dead }}</ref>
